title: Pointwise local-ring dimension inequality for locally quasi-finite algebraic-space morphisms
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $U$ an $S$-scheme, $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and $f:U\to X$ a representable morphism, with point sets [def-a1-space-point-topology]. For an algebraic space $Z$ and a point $z\in|Z|$, write $\delta_Z(z)$ for the dimension of its local ring, namely the common value $\dim\mathcal O_{W,w}$ for an etale morphism $W\to Z$ from a scheme and a point $w$ above $z$; $\mathcal O_{W,w}$ is the stalk of the structure sheaf. Ring dimension is [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] and etale morphisms are [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Assume that $f$ is locally quasi-finite: after every etale scheme chart $V\to X$, the scheme morphism $U\times_XV\to V$ is locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite]; the fibre product is the sheaf fibre product, represented by a scheme by representability. Then for every $u\in U$ one has $$\dim\mathcal O_{U,u}\leq\delta_X(f(u)).$$ No quasi-separatedness, quasi-compactness, or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0ABW, lemma-dimension-local-ring-quasi-finite. The chart definition and scheme agreement are spaces-properties.tex, Tag 04NA (definition-dimension-local-ring) and Tag 0BAM (lemma-pre-dimension-local-ring).

proof.text: Fix $u\in U$. Choose a representable surjective etale atlas $p:V\to X$ from the definition [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Its scheme test along $f$ is $P=U\times_XV$, a scheme with surjective etale projection $a:P\to U$. Choose $w\in P$ over $u$, and put $v=b(w)$ for the other projection $b:P\to V$. The fibre-product relation gives $p(v)=f(u)$. By the hypothesis on $f$, $b$ is locally quasi-finite. These are direct applications of representable surjectivity and etaleness on the scheme test $U$.

source.place: Tag 0ABW (lemma-dimension-local-ring-quasi-finite), proof: etale charts and reduction to Algebra Tag 00QF.

proof.text: Unfold quasi-finiteness of $b$ at $w$ using [pqf-def-quasifinite]. It supplies affine neighbourhoods $\operatorname{Spec}B\subset P$ of $w$ and $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset V$ of $v$, with the former mapped into the latter, for which $A\to B$ is finite type and quasi-finite at the prime $\mathfrak q$ of $w$. Its contraction $\mathfrak p$ is the prime of $v$.

source.place: Tag 01TD (definition-quasi-finite), affine neighbourhoods in the definition of quasi-finite at a point.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-inequality-quasi-finite] to $A\to B$, $\mathfrak q$, and $\mathfrak p$: it gives $\dim B_{\mathfrak q}\leq\dim A_{\mathfrak p}$. The affine-open stalk identifications in [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] identify these rings with $\mathcal O_{P,w}$ and $\mathcal O_{V,v}$, respectively. Ring isomorphisms carry strict prime chains bijectively to strict prime chains, so $$\dim\mathcal O_{P,w}\leq\dim\mathcal O_{V,v}.$$

source.place: Tag 00QF (lemma-dimension-inequality-quasi-finite), applied in the final sentence of the proof of Tag 0ABW.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-space-local-dimension-chart-invariance] for the etale chart $a:P\to U$ and the identity chart of the scheme $U$: $\dim\mathcal O_{P,w}=\dim\mathcal O_{U,u}$. For the etale chart $p:V\to X$ at $v$, the same node gives $\dim\mathcal O_{V,v}=\delta_X(f(u))$. Substituting both equalities in step 3 proves the asserted inequality. Since $u$ was arbitrary this proves every pointwise assertion, including the vacuous case $U=\varnothing$.

Step 2 unfolds 01TD into affine A->B, finite type and quasi-finite at q. Step 3 applies 00QF; all its hypotheses come from step 2, and the stalk-localization leaf (c) gives O ~ localization. Step 4 uses the new node: the scheme clause for U and the chart clauses for a:P->U and p:V->X. This treats h_U as an algebraic space, which the item statement already does, so it adds no gap. Its statement is self-contained and true without Noetherian or quasi-separated hypotheses (via 04N8/07QP); I tested it on Spec k, A^1, infinite-rank valuation rings and the empty space.
